_comment_boundary: Entry: seeded from S10c-exit (arrival at Old Mill Crossing). Covers the walk to the Tether Relay (31,500 budget frames), the Burrow Warrens revisit (65,250 budget frames) and the walk to the South Bridge (54,000 budget frames) = 150,750 frames of movement. Frame budget including boot overhead (~11,500) and this sub-segment's own save-out (~500) is roughly 162,750 frames. At the quiet per-frame rate this run actually measured before combat (0.017-0.028 s/frame) this prices at 2,767-4,557 s (19-32% of the 14,400 s ceiling); at the doubled conservative estimate (0.05 s/frame) it is 8,138 s (56%). Same honest caveat as S10c: this is an extrapolation from a shorter measured quiet period, not a direct measurement of a walk this long.

steps.title: how this segment is entered

args.text: This is the FOURTH of S10's five split sub-segments (S10a..S10e; see S10a.json's header). Its entry save is `S10c-exit`, a split-introduced handoff (arrival at Old Mill Crossing) rather than one section B names in the original monolithic file. The three steps below are the standard handoff mechanics used at every S0n boundary: wipe, seed, boot, Load.

steps.title: empty the live save directory
steps.expected: every slot file is gone, so the seeded slot 4 is the only thing the title's Load list can offer

steps.title: seed slot 4 from the previous sub-segment's exit save
steps.expected: Section B's handoff pattern, applied at this split-introduced boundary: the next segment boots fresh, restores S10c's exit file into `user://`, and loads it through the production title-screen Load path

steps.title: boot the real title screen
steps.expected: the real title comes up with Start New Game focused and Load Game enabled, because a save now exists

steps.expected: d-pad down moves focus from Start New Game to Load Game

steps.title: open the slot list
steps.expected: Load Game opens the slot list and auto-focuses the first non-empty slot, which is the seeded slot 4

steps.expected: the slot loads and the title transitions into the Meadows; section I.4 records the load duration

steps.expected: a cold Meadows stand-up costs about 90 s of CPU on this container -- 466k scattered props and a terrain build -- and every assertion after this reads a live Player

steps.expected: RIG-11: a load restores the party and deploys nothing. No combat is expected in this sub-segment, but the deploy is kept for consistency with every other S0n entry and because a wild encounter along the walk-back is not ruled out.

steps.title: the belt survived the handoff
steps.expected: five of five, unchanged since S10c
steps.observation: RIG-15: equals -> min. Catching is probabilistic; a script's single throw can miss on a real, non-buggy roll, and a team that ends up BIGGER than the milestone is still a team that reached it. `equals` failed both directions for no reason a real player's outcome should fail on.

steps.title: the walk-back is still tracked
steps.expected: Section E.5 objective 27/27, unchanged since S10c. Surviving the S10c/S10d handoff is itself evidence that the flag persisted through a real save/load

steps.title: walk back through the Tether Relay
steps.expected: Section E.6.14: 'Revisit completed areas: ... relay after clearing; record what re-offers, what is correctly spent, what dialogue acknowledges progress'
steps.observation: answer_prompts turned ON for this journey walk. TRADE RECORDED EXPLICITLY: the schema says this flag must stay off in any segment whose subject is whether something blocks travel, so these segments can no longer evidence 'a narrative modal blocked the player from travelling'. That finding is already captured in full, un-answered, in S02-superseded-2/3/4 and S02/BLOCKER.md -- three press counts, identical 7201-frame holds. What it buys is everything downstream: measured in S03 and S04, an unanswered modal at a walk's end left input_context='narrative_modal' where the next step expected combat, so no fight started, no catch resolved, the team never reached three, and every tournament entry check then failed on team size. Without this the journey produces no combat, catching, building or progression evidence at all.

steps.title: the world owns input before this walk

steps.observation: T2-GATEF-RUN6 modal-holds-locomotion audit. A walk that begins while a narrative modal still owns input does not fail as 'a modal is open' -- it fails as 'did not reach', many steps and sometimes many minutes later, which is how X04 lost its whole combat block to 3601 held frames. This assert is diagnostic and changes no behaviour: it turns that silent cascade into one named cause at the point of origin. RIG-25's rule, applied to narrative modals rather than to shop panels.

steps.title: Section B save handoff

args.text: This is a SPLIT-introduced handoff point -- arrival at the South Bridge, a quiet state and the same landmark that separates S05/S06 on the outbound journey. The steps below save it, driven as a player drives it -- the pause shell (opened via the `map` shortcut, RIG-14's deterministic starting point), three RB presses to the Save tab, focus down to slot 4, and the slot's own Save button. `save_out` afterwards only copies the artefact; it saves nothing itself.

steps.expected: a note event carries this observation into events.jsonl

steps.title: open the pause shell
steps.expected: the game_menu button, sent as a real physical event, opens the pause shell; the `map` shortcut is used because it is one of only two tabs with a shortcut in data/config/menu.json and is therefore a deterministic starting point regardless of whatever tab a previous menu use left open (RIG-14)

steps.title: cycle right to the Save tab
steps.expected: three RB presses move from Map (index 2) to Save (index 5) in data/config/menu.json's tab order

steps.title: the Save tab is up
steps.expected: input_context names the live tab: menu_save

steps.title: move focus to slot 4's Save button
steps.expected: focus starts on slot 0's Save button (tab_save.gd::first_focus) and four d-pad downs reach slot 4's

steps.title: press Save
steps.expected: the focused Save button activates and writes slot 4 -- the handoff slot; autosave is slot 0 and slots 1-3 stay free for natural play coverage

steps.title: give the write a moment
steps.expected: the slot file is on disk and section I.4 has timed the save operation

steps.title: copy slot 4 out into the run directory
steps.expected: the resulting `user://` slot file is copied into the run directory as `saves/S10d-exit.json`, for S10e to seed from

steps.title: close the shell
steps.expected: closes the shell and hands the world back

steps.title: this sub-segment is complete
